name: Dawn of the Gods
desc: Before canon, before prophets. Gods are local — river, harvest, ancestor. Each valley its own sanctuary.

events.name: Epic of Gilgamesh composed
events.desc: The first great religious literature: a Sumerian king's quest for immortality. The text's flood narrative will echo through every later Near Eastern religion including the Hebrew Bible.

events.name: Pyramid of Djoser
events.desc: Imhotep designs the first monumental stone religious architecture. The step pyramid at Saqqara makes the pharaoh's afterlife journey visible in stone.

events.name: Stonehenge sarsen ring raised
events.desc: The great stone circle takes its final form. Its solar alignments encode a cosmology whose priests left no texts.

polities.name: Mesopotamian Polytheism
polities.desc: An, Enlil, Enki. Temple-economies run by priesthoods that maintain cosmic order through sacrifice and ritual.

polities.name: Egyptian Polytheism
polities.desc: Ra, Osiris, Isis. The pharaoh as divine intermediary; an elaborate funerary theology written into stone.

polities.name: Indus Valley Religion
polities.desc: Seal imagery of proto-Shiva, sacred baths, fertility cults. The texts remain undeciphered.

polities.name: Chinese Ancestor Worship
polities.desc: Oracle bones, royal divination, reverence for ancestors as intercessors with Heaven (Shangdi).

polities.name: Aegean Polytheism
polities.desc: Cycladic figurines, bull cults, fertility goddesses — predecessors of Minoan and later Greek pantheon.

polities.name: European Megalithic Cults
polities.desc: Stone circles, passage tombs, solar alignments. A ritual landscape whose doctrines are irretrievable.

polities.name: Indigenous Traditions
polities.desc: Most of the planet: oral cosmologies tied to land, lineage, and seasonal cycles. No canon, no clergy, continuous practice.

name: Vedic Dawn
desc: The Vedas begin to be composed on the Indo-Gangetic plain. Akhenaten briefly imposes solar monotheism on Egypt. The Bronze Age cosmos is still a world of local gods and divine kings.

events.name: Rigveda composed
events.desc: The oldest surviving Vedic hymns. Agni, Indra, Soma — the poetry of a semi-nomadic Indo-Aryan priesthood that will become Hinduism.

events.name: Akhenaten's monotheism
events.desc: Pharaoh Amenhotep IV reforms Egyptian religion around worship of the Aten alone, builds a new capital at Amarna. After his death the old gods are restored and his monuments erased — the first attempted monotheism fails utterly.

events.name: Exodus tradition
events.desc: Whatever historical core — a small group leaves Egypt, covenants at Sinai with a desert god who demands exclusive worship. The narrative becomes the founding trauma of Israelite monotheism.

events.name: Moses and the Torah
events.desc: Traditional attribution of the first five books of the Hebrew Bible. Whether Moses is historical, the Torah crystallizes the memory of covenant, law, and a jealous God who permits no rivals.

polities.name: Vedic Religion
polities.desc: Fire altars, Sanskrit hymns, the Rig Veda. Indra, Agni, Soma. The sacrifice is the cosmos.

polities.name: Egyptian Polytheism (New Kingdom)
polities.desc: Amun-Ra ascendant. Akhenaten will briefly proclaim Aten as the sole god before Tutankhamun restores the old cult.

polities.name: Mesopotamian Polytheism
polities.desc: Marduk rising. The Enuma Elish codifies Babylon's gods into the standard Near Eastern pantheon.

polities.name: Hittite Polytheism
polities.desc: A 'thousand gods of Hatti' — Anatolian, Hurrian, and Mesopotamian deities in a syncretic court pantheon.

polities.name: Minoan / Mycenaean
polities.desc: Linear B inscriptions reveal Zeus, Poseidon, and Dionysus already worshipped a millennium before Homer.

polities.name: Canaanite Polytheism
polities.desc: El, Baal, Asherah. The Ugaritic texts preserve the religious world from which Hebrew monotheism will emerge.

polities.name: Shang Ancestor Cult
polities.desc: Oracle-bone divination and royal sacrifice to ancestors. The Shang king is priest as well as sovereign.

polities.name: Celtic / Proto-European
polities.desc: Warrior-aristocratic cults, sacred groves, votive deposits in rivers and bogs.

polities.name: Indigenous Traditions
polities.desc: Oral cosmologies across the Americas, Africa, Oceania, Siberia. Religion without clergy or canon.

name: The Axial Age
desc: A single century produces Confucius, the Buddha, the Hebrew prophets, Greek philosophy, and Zoroaster's reforms. The first religions of interior conscience appear almost simultaneously from the Ganges to the Aegean.

events.name: The Buddha's enlightenment
events.desc: Siddhartha Gautama awakens under the bodhi tree at Bodh Gaya. Dukkha, anatta, the Eightfold Path — a diagnosis of suffering without recourse to gods. Buddhism begins. Traditional date; many scholars place it c. 450 BCE.

events.name: Confucius teaching
events.desc: Kong Qiu travels between the courts of the Spring and Autumn states teaching ren, li, junzi — virtue through ritual and relationship. His Analects will organize Chinese civilization for 2500 years.

events.name: Laozi and the Dao De Jing
events.desc: Traditional date of the foundational Daoist text. Wu wei, the uncarved block, water as the teacher of power. The mystical counterpart to Confucian order.

events.name: Zarathustra's reforms
events.desc: Ahura Mazda against Angra Mainyu — the first systematic dualism of good and evil, with a final judgment and bodily resurrection. Zoroastrianism's vocabulary will flow into Judaism, Christianity, and Islam.

events.name: Babylonian Exile
events.desc: Nebuchadnezzar destroys Jerusalem and deports the Judean elite to Babylon. In exile the Torah is compiled; Yahweh becomes the universal creator rather than a tribal god; a synagogue-and-text religion replaces the cult of the temple.

polities.name: Early Hinduism (Upanishads)
polities.desc: The Upanishads turn Vedic sacrifice inward — Brahman, Atman, moksha. The beginning of Indian philosophy.

polities.name: Early Buddhism
polities.desc: Siddhartha Gautama attains enlightenment; the Four Noble Truths and the Eightfold Path are taught across the Gangetic plain.

polities.name: Jainism
polities.desc: Mahavira, the 24th tirthankara, teaches strict non-violence, asceticism, and karmic liberation.

polities.name: Confucianism
polities.desc: Confucius teaches the Analects — ritual, filial piety, humane government. His disciples carry the doctrine through the Warring States.

polities.name: Taoism (early)
polities.desc: The Dao De Jing is being compiled. The Way that can be named is not the eternal Way.

polities.name: Zoroastrianism
polities.desc: Ahura Mazda versus Angra Mainyu. The first religion to center a cosmic ethical dualism — and the world's first state religion.

polities.name: Second Temple Judaism
polities.desc: The Babylonian exile has just ended. Ezra and Nehemiah codify the Torah. YHWH alone, imageless, covenantal.

polities.name: Greek Polytheism & Philosophy
polities.desc: Homeric gods still central, but Parmenides, Heraclitus, and Pythagoras are already inventing metaphysics.

polities.name: Roman / Etruscan Polytheism
polities.desc: The Roman Republic's state cult — augurs, Vestals, the Capitoline triad. Religion as civic duty, not interior faith.

polities.name: Egyptian Polytheism (late)
polities.desc: Under Persian rule but the old theology endures. Isis, Osiris, and the funerary cult remain central.

polities.name: Celtic Polytheism
polities.desc: Druids, sacred oaks, the cult of the severed head. An oral priesthood leaving almost no texts.

polities.name: Indigenous Traditions
polities.desc: Most of the world remains in local traditions: Scythian, Siberian, African, American, Oceanic.

name: At the Crossroads
desc: Augustus rules Rome. The Second Temple still stands. Buddhism is reaching China along the Silk Road. The Son of God is about to be born in Bethlehem.

events.name: Birth of Jesus Christ
events.desc: The Incarnation: the eternal Word of God is born of the Virgin Mary in Bethlehem during the last years of Herod the Great — traditionally dated to 1 BC, historically placed around 6–4 BC. God has become man. The angel announces peace on earth; shepherds and magi come to worship the newborn King. From this event Christians reckon time itself; the AD of 'anno Domini,' the year of our Lord, begins here. The empire that will crucify him will, within three centuries, be baptized in his name.

events.name: Resurrection of Christ (Easter)
events.desc: Passover week, AD 30 or 33. Jesus Christ, true God and true man, is crucified under Pontius Pilate, dies, and is buried. On the third day he rises from the dead, appearing to Mary Magdalene, to Peter, to the Twelve, and to more than five hundred witnesses. The Resurrection is the definitive victory over sin and death — the foundation of Christian faith and the reason the Gospel is proclaimed. As Saint Paul writes, 'if Christ has not been raised, our preaching is in vain.' The empty tomb outside Jerusalem is the hinge of history and the reference point of Western dating itself.

events.name: Paul's Missionary Journeys
events.desc: A Pharisee from Tarsus, formerly a persecutor of the Jesus-movement, crosses Anatolia and Greece founding communities from Antioch to Corinth to Rome. His letters, the earliest Christian texts, argue that the gospel is for Gentiles as well as Jews — the decision that transforms a Jewish sect into a world religion.

events.name: Destruction of the Second Temple
events.desc: Titus's legions burn the Jerusalem Temple at the climax of the Jewish Revolt. The sacrificial cult ends forever; rabbinic Judaism — portable, text-based, synagogue-centered — survives the catastrophe and becomes the Jewish religion of the next two millennia. The same year the Jesus-movement definitively separates from its parent tradition.

polities.name: Roman-Hellenistic Polytheism
polities.desc: Jupiter, Mars, the Capitoline triad plus local deities across the empire. The imperial cult binds provinces to the emperor.

polities.name: Second Temple Judaism
polities.desc: Pharisees, Sadducees, Essenes, and apocalyptic sects contend. The Temple still stands; the synagogue is becoming central.

polities.name: Zoroastrianism (Parthian)
polities.desc: The Parthian court's religion. Fire temples dot Iran. The Magi have become a byword across the Mediterranean.

polities.name: Hinduism (Classical)
polities.desc: The Mahabharata and Ramayana are being compiled. Bhakti devotion to Vishnu and Shiva is rising alongside Vedic orthodoxy.

polities.name: Buddhism (Early Mahayana)
polities.desc: Theravada across South Asia; proto-Mahayana emerging in Gandhara. Missionaries reaching China via the Silk Road.

polities.name: Chinese Folk / Confucian / Taoist
polities.desc: Han-dynasty synthesis: Confucian bureaucracy, Taoist mysticism, ancestor worship, emperor as Son of Heaven.

polities.name: Celtic & Germanic Polytheism
polities.desc: Druids suppressed in Gaul, still active in Britain and Ireland. Germanic tribes beyond the Rhine worship Wodan, Thor, and ancestral heroes.

polities.name: Egyptian Polytheism
polities.desc: Isis-worship has spread across the Roman world. Temples still active; Christianity is decades away.

name: Edict of Milan
desc: Constantine legalizes Christianity. Within eighty years it will be the Roman state religion. The hinge on which the Mediterranean tips from pagan antiquity to Christian late antiquity.

events.name: Edict of Milan
events.desc: Constantine and Licinius grant legal toleration to all religions, effectively ending state persecution of Christians. Within 70 years Theodosius will make it the only legal religion.

events.name: Council of Nicaea
events.desc: Constantine convenes 300 bishops to resolve the Arian controversy. The Nicene Creed declares Christ homoousios — of one substance with the Father. The first ecumenical definition of orthodoxy.

events.name: Augustine converts
events.desc: Augustine of Hippo, rhetorician and Manichaean, hears a child's voice — tolle lege — and reads Romans 13. His Confessions and City of God will shape Western Christianity more than any writer after Paul.

events.name: Jerome's Vulgate
events.desc: Jerome completes the Latin translation of the Bible from Hebrew and Greek. The Vulgate will be the West's Bible for a thousand years.

events.name: Theodosius bans paganism
events.desc: The Theodosian decrees outlaw all non-Christian sacrifice, close temples, and end the Olympic Games. Christianity becomes the state religion of the Roman Empire.

polities.name: Christianity (nascent)
polities.desc: Recently legalized; still a minority. Bishops at Rome, Antioch, Alexandria, Jerusalem are already contesting doctrine — the Arian controversy is brewing.

polities.name: Roman-Hellenistic Polytheism
polities.desc: Still the religion of most Romans. Will be formally disestablished by Theodosius in 392.

polities.name: Zoroastrianism (Sasanian)
polities.desc: The Sasanian state religion, aggressively defended against Christian and Manichaean encroachment.

polities.name: Manichaeism
polities.desc: Mani's third-century synthesis of Zoroastrian, Christian, and Buddhist elements. Spreading from North Africa to China along the Silk Road.

polities.name: Hinduism
polities.desc: Gupta classical age approaching. Temple Hinduism, Puranic mythology, and the great philosophical schools all flourishing.

polities.name: Buddhism
polities.desc: Theravada in South/SE Asia; Mahayana spreading across China and Central Asia. The great monastic universities are being founded.

polities.name: Chinese Folk / Taoist / Confucian
polities.desc: Buddhism is still a foreign import. Native traditions — Confucian rites, Taoist alchemy, ancestral worship — remain dominant at every level.

polities.name: Judaism
polities.desc: Diaspora Judaism after the Temple's destruction. The Palestinian and Babylonian Talmuds are being composed. Rabbinic Judaism is consolidating.

polities.name: Celtic & Germanic Polytheism
polities.desc: Rhine and Danube still frontier. Germanic confederacies, British druidic remnants, and Irish pre-Christian culture still dominant.

polities.name: Indigenous Traditions
polities.desc: The Americas, sub-Saharan Africa, Oceania, most of Siberia, and the steppe still in local traditions.

name: The Hijra
desc: Muhammad's flight from Mecca to Medina. Year 1 of the Islamic calendar. Within a century Islam will command Iberia to the Indus — the fastest territorial expansion of any religion in history.

events.name: The Hijra
events.desc: Muhammad and the early Muslims flee Mecca for Yathrib (Medina). The year becomes year one of the Islamic calendar. The umma — the community of believers — is founded.

events.name: Conquest of Mecca
events.desc: Muhammad returns at the head of 10,000 men. The Kaaba is cleansed of idols. Arabia unifies under Islam within two years of his death.

events.name: Caliph Umar takes Jerusalem
events.desc: The second Rashidun caliph enters the holy city on foot. The Dome of the Rock will rise in 691 on the Temple Mount. Jerusalem enters its long Islamic chapter.

events.name: Early Muslim Conquests
events.desc: The Rashidun armies break both great powers of late antiquity in a single decade. At Yarmouk (636) they shatter a Byzantine army and take Syria and Palestine. At al-Qadisiyyah (636) they destroy the Sasanian field army; by 651 the last Sasanian shah is dead and Persia — the rival of Rome for seven centuries — is gone forever. Egypt falls in 641; the Exarchate of Africa by 698. In sixty years an Arab desert people ruled from Tripoli to the Oxus. Nothing in the history of religion or war moves this fast again until the Mongols.

events.name: Umayyad Conquest of Iberia
events.desc: Tariq ibn Ziyad crosses from Africa at the rock that will bear his name — Gibraltar, Jabal Tariq. Within seven years the Umayyads destroy the Visigothic kingdom and rule most of the peninsula. Al-Andalus will be a center of Muslim civilization for nearly eight hundred years; the Reconquista that ends it will not conclude until 1492.

events.name: Battle of Tours
events.desc: Charles Martel halts the Umayyad advance into Francia. Islamic expansion into Western Europe peaks and reverses. Christendom retains the Frankish heartland.

polities.name: Islam (nascent)
polities.desc: Muhammad and his followers at Medina. Within ten years Arabia will be unified under Islam; within a century, half the Roman-Sasanian world.

polities.name: Eastern (Orthodox) Christianity
polities.desc: The Byzantine state religion. Just emerged exhausted from two decades of war with Sasanian Persia — about to lose Syria, Egypt, and North Africa to Islam.

polities.name: Western (Catholic) Christianity
polities.desc: The papacy is asserting itself as the spiritual head of Western Christendom. Ireland and Iberia are now Christian; Anglo-Saxon England is being converted.

polities.name: Zoroastrianism (Sasanian, terminal)
polities.desc: The state religion of a Sasanian empire that has about twenty years left before Arab Muslim armies end it.

polities.name: Hinduism
polities.desc: Harsha's north Indian empire; bhakti poetry flourishing in the Tamil south. Buddhism is still present but in slow decline.

polities.name: Buddhism
polities.desc: Xuanzang's pilgrimage from China to India begins this year. Tang China, Silla Korea, Nara Japan all Buddhist. Tibet converts next century.

polities.name: Chinese Taoist / Confucian
polities.desc: Tang dynasty supports all three teachings — Confucian rites for the state, Taoist for the emperor, Buddhist for the people.

polities.name: Shinto (proto)
polities.desc: The Yamato court venerates Amaterasu and the kami of mountains, rivers, and ancestors. Buddhism arriving from Korea is beginning to blend in.

polities.name: Germanic & Slavic Polytheism
polities.desc: Wotan and Thor in Scandinavia and German lands east of the Rhine. Slavic Perun-worship across Eastern Europe. Christianity pressing from Ireland and Constantinople.

polities.desc: The Americas, sub-Saharan Africa, Oceania, Siberia still untouched by world religions.

name: The Great Schism
desc: Pope Leo IX and Patriarch Michael Cerularius mutually excommunicate. Latin and Greek Christianity formally split. The break will outlast both their lifetimes by a thousand years.

events.name: The Great Schism
events.desc: Cardinal Humbert places a bull of excommunication on the altar of Hagia Sophia. Patriarch Michael Cerularius returns the favor. The filioque, papal primacy, unleavened bread — a millennium of drift ends in formal break.

events.name: Cluniac Reform
events.desc: The Abbey of Cluny leads a revival of Benedictine discipline, liberation of monasteries from lay control, and a vision of papal monarchy that will climax in Gregory VII.

events.name: Conversion of Vladimir
events.desc: Vladimir of Kiev chooses Byzantine Christianity after dispatching envoys to test Islam, Latin Christianity, Judaism, and Orthodoxy. The mass baptism in the Dnieper makes Rus' Orthodox — a choice Russia is still living with.

polities.name: Catholic Christianity
polities.desc: Latin Christendom under papal primacy. The Gregorian reforms are about to begin; the First Crusade is forty-five years away.

polities.name: Orthodox Christianity
polities.desc: The Byzantine church plus Kievan Rus' (converted 988), Bulgaria, Serbia. The Byzantine emperor is still the senior Christian ruler.

polities.name: Sunni Islam
polities.desc: The Abbasid caliphate in political decline, but the religious mainstream. Seljuk Turks have just taken Baghdad and are about to reshape the Muslim world.

polities.name: Shia Islam (Fatimid)
polities.desc: The Fatimid caliphate rules Egypt and the Levant as a rival Shia caliphate. Within a century Saladin will end it.

polities.name: Hinduism
polities.desc: The Chola Empire rules the south; the Pala are patronizing Buddhism in Bengal. Bhakti saints compose Tamil devotional poetry.

polities.name: Buddhism
polities.desc: Song-era Chan (Zen) flourishing in China; Tendai and Shingon in Japan; Theravada throughout Southeast Asia; Tibetan Vajrayana crystallizing.

polities.name: Chinese Taoist / Confucian
polities.desc: Neo-Confucianism is crystallizing under Zhou Dunyi and the Cheng brothers, synthesizing Confucian ethics with Buddhist and Taoist metaphysics.

polities.name: Germanic / Slavic Polytheism (remnant)
polities.desc: Iceland converts in 1000; Sweden's last pagan king is a generation away. Baltic and Finnic peoples and some Slavic tribes still pagan.

polities.name: Indigenous Traditions
polities.desc: The Americas (Maya, Toltec, early Mississippian), sub-Saharan Africa (ex-Sahel), Oceania, Siberia still in local traditions. West Africa beginning to Islamize.

name: First Crusade
desc: Jerusalem falls to the Crusaders. The first sustained military contact between Latin Christendom and the Islamic world since Charles Martel. Banking, algebra, paper, and philosophy will flow west through the wounds the Crusades open.

events.name: Council of Clermont
events.desc: Urban II preaches the First Crusade. Deus vult. A response to a Byzantine request for mercenaries becomes an armed pilgrimage that will take Jerusalem in four years.

events.name: Siege of Jerusalem
events.desc: Crusader forces take Jerusalem after five weeks and massacre the inhabitants. The Kingdom of Jerusalem is established. Christian Europe, for the first and last time, holds the holy city.

events.name: Founding of the Cistercians
events.desc: Robert of Molesme founds Cîteaux in the Burgundian marshes. Bernard of Clairvaux will make the order the most powerful monastic movement in Europe, draining swamps, preaching crusades, shaping kings.

events.name: Saladin retakes Jerusalem
events.desc: After the rout at Hattin, Saladin enters Jerusalem. Unlike the Christians of 1099, he does not massacre. The Third Crusade will not recover the city.

polities.name: Catholic Christianity
polities.desc: The First Crusade has just taken Jerusalem. Crusader states on the Levantine coast will last two centuries. Latin Christendom discovers Islam as rival and teacher.

polities.name: Orthodox Christianity
polities.desc: Alexios I Komnenos has called for Western help against the Seljuks and got a Crusade he did not expect. The empire is recovering.

polities.name: Sunni Islam (Seljuk)
polities.desc: The Seljuk Turks hold Baghdad and most of the Sunni heartland. Their fragmentation into quarreling atabegs is why the First Crusade has succeeded.

polities.name: Shia Islam (Fatimid, twilight)
polities.desc: The Fatimids have just lost Jerusalem and the coastal Levant. Will fall to Saladin's Ayyubid dynasty in 1171.

polities.name: Hinduism
polities.desc: Chola maritime dominance in the Indian Ocean. Ghaznavid raiders from Afghanistan are beginning the long Islamic incursion into the subcontinent.

polities.name: Buddhism
polities.desc: Angkor Wat is being planned as a Hindu-Buddhist temple. Japanese Pure Land is emerging. Tibet's second dissemination is consolidating.

polities.name: Chinese Neo-Confucianism
polities.desc: Zhu Xi (b. 1130) will synthesize a thousand years of Confucian, Taoist, and Buddhist thought into the orthodoxy that shapes East Asia until the 20th century.

polities.name: Indigenous Traditions
polities.desc: The Americas, sub-Saharan Africa beyond the Sahel, Oceania, Siberia.

name: Eve of the Reformation
desc: Columbus has reached the Caribbean. Portuguese ships are rounding Africa. Martin Luther is seventeen years old. The religious map of the planet is about to be redrawn by both printing press and caravel.

events.name: Fall of Constantinople
events.desc: Mehmed II's cannons breach the Theodosian walls. Hagia Sophia becomes a mosque. The Eastern Roman Empire ends; Moscow will claim the title of Third Rome.

events.name: Savonarola's Bonfire
events.desc: The Dominican friar's followers burn books, paintings, and luxuries in the Piazza della Signoria. A year later Savonarola himself is burned. The prelude to Reformation fire-and-brimstone.

events.name: Spanish Inquisition begins
events.desc: Ferdinand and Isabella establish the Tribunal of the Holy Office. Conversos, moriscos, Protestants, mystics — the instrument of religious enforcement that will outlast the empire that built it.

polities.name: Catholic Christianity
polities.desc: Still the unified Western church. The papacy of Alexander VI embodies both the cultural peak and the institutional rot that will split Europe.

polities.name: Orthodox Christianity
polities.desc: Moscow proclaims itself the 'Third Rome' after Constantinople's 1453 fall. Russian Orthodoxy becomes the church's political center of gravity.

polities.name: Sunni Islam
polities.desc: The Ottomans rule Constantinople, Egypt coming next. Timurid Persia is fragmenting. From Morocco to Bengal, Sunni Islam is the religion of state.

polities.name: Shia Islam (emerging Safavid)
polities.desc: Shah Ismail will conquer Iran next year and declare Twelver Shiism the state religion, fixing the Sunni-Shia divide on the political map to the present day.

polities.name: Hinduism
polities.desc: The Vijayanagara empire anchors the Hindu south against Muslim sultanates. Chaitanya's Gaudiya Vaishnavism is emerging in Bengal.

polities.name: Buddhism
polities.desc: Theravada dominant in Southeast Asia; Gelugpa reforming Tibetan Buddhism; Zen flourishing in Japan. Buddhism has almost vanished from India itself.

polities.name: Chinese Neo-Confucianism
polities.desc: Ming-dynasty orthodoxy. Wang Yangming is a child; his idealist school will shake the Zhu Xi synthesis within thirty years.

polities.name: Indigenous Traditions
polities.desc: The Americas are being invaded but most of them still practice pre-contact religion. Sub-Saharan Africa, Oceania, Siberia, northern Japan (Ainu) unchanged.

name: The Reformation
desc: Luther posts the Ninety-Five Theses at Wittenberg. Within a generation Latin Christendom is permanently split. The religious wars that follow will kill millions and, by exhausting everyone, produce the modern secular state.

events.name: 95 Theses
events.desc: Martin Luther posts (or mails) his theses against indulgences to the Archbishop of Mainz. Whether nailed to the church door or not, the printing press makes them the first viral religious text. Western Christianity splits.

events.name: Diet of Worms
events.desc: Luther refuses to recant before Charles V. Hier stehe ich, ich kann nicht anders. He is declared an outlaw; Frederick the Wise hides him at the Wartburg where he translates the New Testament into German.

events.name: Henry VIII breaks from Rome
events.desc: The Act of Supremacy declares Henry VIII 'Supreme Head of the Church of England,' severing the English Church from papal jurisdiction over his divorce from Catherine of Aragon. A political rupture that becomes a theological one: within a century the Church of England produces Cranmer's Book of Common Prayer, the King James Bible, and an Anglican middle way between Rome and Geneva.

events.name: Council of Trent
events.desc: The Counter-Reformation's defining council. Transubstantiation reaffirmed, the Vulgate canonized, seminaries established. Catholicism becomes what it will be until Vatican II.

events.name: Society of Jesus founded
events.desc: Ignatius of Loyola and his companions receive papal approval. The Jesuits will be the pope's shock troops — in education, in missions from Japan to Paraguay, in the Counter-Reformation campaign.

events.name: Moscow gets its own patriarch, and the charter calls Russia the Third Rome
events.desc: Jeremias II of Constantinople made Job the first Patriarch of Moscow in 1589, in a charter that calls Russia the Third Rome. It put Moscow's claim to Byzantium's Orthodox mantle in writing.

polities.name: Catholic Christianity
polities.desc: Still the religion of most Western Christians. The Counter-Reformation is thirty years away; the Council of Trent will codify distinctive Catholic doctrine by 1563.

polities.name: Protestant Christianity (nascent)
polities.desc: Luther in Saxony; Zwingli in Zurich. Calvin is an eight-year-old in Picardy. The Reformation is this year; the permanence of the split will become clear by 1555.

polities.name: Orthodox Christianity
polities.desc: Moscow's 'Third Rome' doctrine consolidates. Russian Orthodox autocephaly is formalized in 1589.

polities.name: Mixed: Catholic north, Orthodox south, Muslim elite
polities.desc: Albania under early Ottoman rule: Catholic in the north, Orthodox in the south, with a small converting Muslim elite. Tax registers show most districts under 5% Muslim.

polities.name: Sunni Islam
polities.desc: Selim the Grim has just conquered Egypt and claimed the caliphate. Suleiman the Magnificent will drive Ottoman power to its peak.

polities.name: Shia Islam (Safavid Iran)
polities.desc: Shah Ismail's dynasty has fixed Shiism as Iran's state religion. The Ottoman-Safavid rivalry will define the Islamic world for two centuries.

polities.name: Ibadi Islam
polities.desc: Oman's Ibadi tradition, neither Sunni nor Shia, rooted in the first-century Kharijite split. The imamate and later the Ya'aruba and Al Said rulers are Ibadi.

polities.name: Hinduism
polities.desc: Vijayanagara at its peak under Krishnadevaraya; Mughal invasion of the north is nine years away. Bhakti poetry flourishing across the subcontinent.

polities.name: Buddhism
polities.desc: Theravada dominant in Southeast Asia; Tibetan Buddhism spreading among Mongols. Japan's warrior monasteries will be crushed by Oda Nobunaga later in the century.

polities.name: Chinese Neo-Confucianism
polities.desc: Wang Yangming's mind-based revision is challenging the Zhu Xi orthodoxy. The exam system still binds the empire together.

polities.name: Indigenous Traditions
polities.desc: Aztec and Inca empires practice state religion two years from catastrophic contact. Most of sub-Saharan Africa, Oceania, Siberia, and pre-contact Americas still in local traditions.

name: Confessional World
desc: A century and a half of religious war has settled Europe into Protestant north and Catholic south. Catholic missions have baptized Latin America. The Jesuits are in Beijing. The Dutch are in Nagasaki. The Enlightenment is beginning.

events.name: Peace of Westphalia
events.desc: Cuius regio, eius religio. The wars of religion end by granting each sovereign the right to determine his subjects' confession. The modern state system is born out of religious exhaustion.

events.name: Great Awakening
events.desc: Jonathan Edwards and George Whitefield ignite a revival that sweeps the American colonies. Heartfelt conversion, itinerant preaching, mass emotion — the template for American evangelicalism.

events.name: Wesley's conversion
events.desc: John Wesley feels his heart 'strangely warmed' at a Moravian meeting on Aldersgate Street. Methodism is born. The industrial working class will get a religion that works for them.

polities.name: Catholic Christianity
polities.desc: The Iberian empires have made Catholicism the majority religion of the Americas and the Philippines. Jesuit missions reach Beijing, Kyoto, and Mughal courts. In North America, New France along the St. Lawrence and Acadia are French Catholic; Spanish Florida and New Mexico are Spanish Catholic; Maryland was founded as a Catholic proprietary colony.

polities.name: Protestant Christianity
polities.desc: Anglican England, Calvinist Netherlands, Lutheran Scandinavia. Pilgrim New England — a thin coastal strip of British colonies from New Hampshire to the Carolinas. The Enlightenment and the commercial revolution incubate within Protestant societies.

polities.name: Orthodox Christianity
polities.desc: Peter the Great subordinates the church to the state via the Holy Synod in 1721. Russian Orthodoxy becomes a department of the imperial government.

polities.name: Sunni Islam
polities.desc: Three great Muslim empires — Ottoman, Safavid, Mughal — span Morocco to Bengal. The Ottoman decline has begun; Aurangzeb's Mughal India is at its peak but fraying.

polities.name: Shia Islam
polities.desc: The Safavid dynasty's last stable decade before Afghan invaders sack Isfahan in 1722. Shia clerical institutions in Najaf and Karbala are independent of the crown.

polities.name: Ibadi Islam
polities.desc: Oman's Ibadi tradition, neither Sunni nor Shia, rooted in the first-century Kharijite split. The imamate and later the Ya'aruba and Al Said rulers are Ibadi.

polities.name: Hinduism
polities.desc: The Marathas are rising as the great Hindu challenge to Mughal rule. Hindu temple towns remain the cultural centers of the subcontinent.

polities.name: Sikhism
polities.desc: Guru Gobind Singh founds the Khalsa in 1699. Sikhism is crystallizing into a distinct martial religious community in the Punjab.

polities.name: Buddhism
polities.desc: The Fifth Dalai Lama's Potala is complete. Tokugawa Japan registers the population through Buddhist temples. Theravada revitalized in Ayutthaya and Burma.

polities.name: Chinese Neo-Confucianism
polities.desc: The Qing Kangxi Emperor — Manchu by descent — has become the model Confucian scholar-ruler. Jesuits serve at court as astronomers.

polities.name: Indigenous Traditions
polities.desc: Sub-Saharan Africa beyond the Sahel, Oceania, Siberian peoples, the North American interior, and Amazonia still practice pre-contact religion. Everything west of the Appalachian British colonies and north of the Spanish presidio line in New Spain — the entire American heartland, Great Plains, Rocky Mountains, Pacific Northwest, Alaska, and Hawaii — is the continuous territory of the Iroquois, Shawnee, Cherokee, Creek, Muscogee, Lakota, Comanche, Apache, Navajo, Hopi, Pueblo, Nez Perce, Chinook, Tlingit, Aleut, and hundreds of other nations with intact cosmologies.

name: The Secular Turn
desc: The French Revolution disestablishes the Church, declares the Rights of Man, and briefly attempts a Cult of Reason. For the first time a major state grounds its legitimacy in something other than religion. The template for every secular republic to come.

events.name: Clement XIV dissolves the Jesuits after Catholic kings expel them
events.desc: Clement XIV abolished the Society of Jesus in July 1773, after Portugal, France and Spain had expelled it. It showed Catholic crowns could make the papacy abolish one of its own orders.

events.name: Civil Constitution of the Clergy
events.desc: The French Revolution nationalizes church property and makes priests elected state employees. The Pope condemns it; the breach splits French Catholicism and radicalizes the Revolution.

events.name: Cult of the Supreme Being
events.desc: Robespierre stages a festival in the Champ de Mars to inaugurate his deist state religion. Two months later he dies under the guillotine. Revolutionary religion fails.

events.name: Darwin's Origin
events.desc: The Origin of Species proposes natural selection. Within a generation, design arguments lose their hold on educated opinion in the West. The most serious intellectual challenge to religion since the Greeks.

events.name: First Vatican Council
events.desc: Pius IX defines papal infallibility on matters of faith and morals. The pope becomes the authoritative voice of Catholicism in a way he never was before.

polities.name: Catholic Christianity
polities.desc: The Revolution seizes Church property, requires an oath to the state, and drives the papacy into exile. The modern tension between Church and secular state begins here. In British North America, the Quebec Act of 1774 has guaranteed the free practice of Catholicism along the St. Lawrence; Lower Canada and the surviving Acadian communities of New Brunswick remain French Catholic. In the new American republic, Maryland — founded as a haven for English Catholics by Lord Baltimore — remains the one visibly Catholic state.

polities.name: Secular Republic
polities.desc: The National Assembly disestablishes the Church. The Declaration of the Rights of Man grounds authority in the nation, not the divine right of kings. The template for every later secular state.

polities.name: Protestant Christianity
polities.desc: The First Great Awakening has transformed American religion. The US Constitution disestablishes religion at the federal level — the first large-scale experiment in church-state separation. The United States is thirteen coastal states hugging the Atlantic; everything west of the Appalachians is Native, Spanish, British, or French. In British North America, Upper Canada and the Maritimes have just absorbed tens of thousands of Loyalists fleeing the American Revolution, entrenching Anglican and Methodist practice.

polities.name: Orthodox Christianity
polities.desc: The Russian Orthodox church remains a department of the imperial government. Catherine the Great's reforms secularize monastic lands while keeping orthodoxy as state religion.

polities.name: Sunni Islam
polities.desc: The Ottoman Empire is declining but remains the formal seat of the caliphate. Wahhabi reform is gaining ground in Arabia under Muhammad ibn Abd al-Wahhab.

polities.name: Shia Islam
polities.desc: The Qajar dynasty rules Iran. The Shia clerical establishment in the shrine cities of Najaf and Karbala is financially and institutionally autonomous from the state.

polities.name: Ibadi Islam
polities.desc: Oman's Ibadi tradition, neither Sunni nor Shia, rooted in the first-century Kharijite split. The imamate and later the Ya'aruba and Al Said rulers are Ibadi.

polities.name: Hinduism
polities.desc: Mughal power has collapsed. British East India Company is gaining power in Bengal. Hindu reform movements are incubating.

polities.name: Sikhism
polities.desc: Ranjit Singh will consolidate the Sikh Empire in the Punjab within a decade. Sikh political power at its historical peak.

polities.name: Buddhism
polities.desc: Qing China's tribute system links Tibet and Mongolia to Beijing through Buddhist diplomacy. Theravada kingdoms in Southeast Asia consolidate.

polities.name: Chinese Neo-Confucianism
polities.desc: The Qianlong Emperor's reign is near its peak. Confucian state orthodoxy binds the largest, wealthiest empire on earth. Lord Macartney will be rebuffed in four years.

polities.name: Indigenous Traditions
polities.desc: Sub-Saharan Africa, Polynesia, and much of the Americas west of European settlement. The Canadian Shield, Rupert's Land, the prairies, the Rockies, the Pacific Northwest, and the Arctic are entirely First Nations, Métis, and Inuit territory — the Hudson's Bay Company trades through them but has not converted them. Across the new American republic, everything west of the Appalachians remains Indigenous country — Shawnee, Miami, Potawatomi in the Old Northwest; Cherokee, Creek, Chickasaw, Choctaw in the Southeast before removal; Lakota, Crow, Blackfeet on the Great Plains; Navajo, Apache, Hopi, Pueblo in the Southwest; Nez Perce, Chinook on the Columbia; Tlingit in Russian Alaska; Hawaiian Kapu system still intact in the Pacific. Christian and Muslim missions are advancing globally but have not yet supplanted local traditions.

name: State Atheism
desc: The Bolsheviks seize power in Petrograd. Marxism-Leninism becomes the first world-historical ideology since early Islam to attempt the mass replacement of religion itself. By 1950 a third of humanity will live under officially atheist governments.

events.name: Russian Revolution
events.desc: The Bolsheviks seize power and immediately begin dismantling the Russian Orthodox Church — property seized, clergy executed, militant atheism made state doctrine. The first experiment in state-imposed irreligion.

events.name: Scopes Trial
events.desc: Tennessee tries a high-school teacher for teaching evolution. William Jennings Bryan vs Clarence Darrow. American fundamentalism retreats from public prestige and builds its own parallel institutions for the next fifty years.

polities.name: Marxist-Leninist State Atheism
polities.desc: Lenin's Bolsheviks outlaw religious education and seize church property. Orthodox clergy are shot or sent to camps. The first modern state built on the ambition to abolish religion.

polities.name: Catholic Christianity
polities.desc: Pius X's anti-modernist campaign. Benedict XV is negotiating the end of World War I. Mexico is six years into an anticlerical civil war. The Church has lost the Papal States but retains a global institution. Forty years of Irish, Italian, and Polish immigration have made the American Northeast Catholic by plurality; Louisiana remains French-Spanish Catholic; New Mexico remains Hispano-Catholic. Quebec — a distinct French Catholic nation inside the British Empire — is at the height of its ultramontane clerical-nationalist moment.

polities.name: Protestant Christianity
polities.desc: American Protestant missionary movement at its peak. The South, Midwest, and mountain West are solidly Protestant — Baptist, Methodist, Lutheran, Presbyterian. Social Gospel in the cities; Pentecostalism spreading (Azusa Street, 1906). English Canada — Ontario, the Maritimes, the newly settled prairies, and British Columbia — is solidly Anglican, Presbyterian, Methodist, and Baptist. Weimar Germany about to experiment with secular modernism.

polities.name: Orthodox Christianity
polities.desc: The Russian church is being persecuted. Greek, Serbian, Bulgarian, and Romanian churches autocephalous. The Ecumenical Patriarchate in Istanbul is reduced to a symbolic role.

polities.name: Sunni Islam
polities.desc: The Ottoman caliphate has five years left. Arab nationalism is rising against Turkish rule. Al-Azhar in Cairo is consolidating as the leading Sunni religious authority.

polities.name: Shia Islam
polities.desc: The Qajar dynasty is collapsing. The Constitutional Revolution of 1906–11 has politicized the clergy in ways that will shape the century.

polities.name: Hinduism
polities.desc: The Indian independence movement is appropriating Hindu symbols under Tilak and (soon) Gandhi. Hindu reformist movements — Arya Samaj, Ramakrishna Mission — are reshaping tradition.

polities.name: Sikhism
polities.desc: The Singh Sabha movement has standardized Sikh practice. Two years from the Jallianwala Bagh massacre; Sikh political consciousness will become central to Indian independence.

polities.name: Buddhism
polities.desc: Japan's state Shinto is subordinating Buddhism. Modernist Buddhism emerges in Sri Lanka and Japan. Thailand's monarchy reforms the sangha.

polities.name: Chinese Republican Confucianism
polities.desc: The Qing has fallen in 1912 and with it the Confucian exam state. The New Culture Movement is attacking Confucianism as the source of Chinese backwardness.

polities.name: Indigenous Traditions
polities.desc: Colonial missions have dramatically reduced indigenous religious populations, but significant practice persists in sub-Saharan Africa, Amazonia, Oceania, the far Canadian north, and the American frontier reservations. The Inuit of the Arctic, the Dene and Gwich'in of the boreal interior, and the Yukon First Nations remain largely outside regular mission reach. In the United States, Alaska is still overwhelmingly Native (annexed only in 1867); Oklahoma was Indian Territory until statehood in 1907 and retains huge Cherokee, Choctaw, Creek, Chickasaw, and Seminole populations; Navajo Nation in Arizona, the Pueblos in New Mexico, and the Lakota reservations in the Dakotas preserve ceremonial practice even as the Ghost Dance and Native American Church movements emerge.

name: A New Israel
desc: The State of Israel is declared in Tel Aviv. The Chinese Communists are a year from Beijing. Indian partition has displaced fifteen million and killed a million. The postwar religious map is being drawn in blood.

events.name: Declaration of Israel
events.desc: Ben-Gurion reads the declaration in Tel Aviv. The first Jewish state in nineteen centuries. Zionism's theological-political gamble pays off and immediately triggers a war that will not end.

events.name: World Council of Churches
events.desc: Formed in Amsterdam from the ecumenical movement's pre-war work. Protestant and Orthodox churches begin a conversation that would have been unthinkable a generation earlier.

events.name: Billy Graham's Los Angeles Crusade
events.desc: Eight weeks in a tent at Washington and Hill. Hearst wires his papers: 'Puff Graham.' American evangelicalism's great postwar revival begins; Graham will advise every president from Truman to Obama.

polities.name: Marxist-Leninist State Atheism
polities.desc: Stalin's USSR, the Eastern Bloc, and — from 1949 — Mao's PRC all enforce official atheism. At its peak, a third of humanity lives under governments explicitly hostile to religion.

polities.name: Catholic Christianity
polities.desc: Pius XII reigns. Christian Democracy is emerging as a political force in postwar Western Europe. Latin American Catholicism is massively dominant but about to be challenged by Protestantism. In the United States, the urban Northeast is now the largest Catholic population in the world outside of Latin America; New York is also the largest Jewish city ever to exist, with over two million Jews. Quebec remains a priest-ridden society — what Quebec historians will later call the grande noirceur, the Great Darkness — with Duplessis and the clergy governing together.

polities.name: Protestant Christianity
polities.desc: American Protestantism becomes the dominant religious force of the Free World — the Bible Belt, the mainline Northeast, the Midwest, and the West all overwhelmingly Protestant. English Canada (Ontario, the Maritimes, the prairies, British Columbia) is overwhelmingly Anglican and United Church. Billy Graham holds his first crusade in 1949. Postwar ecumenical movement consolidates.

polities.name: Orthodox Christianity
polities.desc: The Russian church, nearly destroyed under Stalin, has been partially restored for the war effort. Greek, Serbian, Bulgarian churches return under Communist control.

polities.name: Sunni Islam
polities.desc: Secular Arab nationalism (Nasser, Ba'ath) is rising against British and French imperial residues. Islamists (Muslim Brotherhood) and secular nationalists will contest the Arab world for fifty years.

polities.name: Shia Islam
polities.desc: Mohammad Reza Shah's Iran is a staunch Cold War ally of the US; the Shia clergy are politically subordinated but growing in social influence. The Islamic Revolution is thirty-one years away.

polities.name: Judaism
polities.desc: The State of Israel is declared on May 14, 1948. The first Jewish state in nearly two thousand years. Jewish populations across the Arab world will migrate over the next two decades.

polities.name: Hinduism
polities.desc: Nehru's secular India is constitutionally pluralist but demographically Hindu. Gandhi has just been assassinated by a Hindu nationalist. Partition has concentrated Hindus in India, Muslims in Pakistan.

polities.name: Buddhism
polities.desc: Tibet's autonomy has one year left. Occupied Japan is de-Shintoized. Southeast Asian Theravada kingdoms are under pressure from Communism and decolonization.

polities.name: Indigenous Traditions
polities.desc: Declining rapidly but still significant in sub-Saharan Africa, the Pacific, parts of Latin America, and the Canadian Arctic — where the residential school system is at its cruelest peak but Inuit and Dene communities retain much traditional practice. Liberation theology will begin to blend Catholicism with indigenous practice.

name: The Return of God
desc: The Iranian Revolution installs a Shia theocracy. The Sandinistas cite Liberation Theology. Moral Majority founded in Virginia. The Soviet Union invades Afghanistan and will be defeated by mujahedeen. After a century of secular ascendancy, political religion returns as the defining force of the decade.

events.name: Iranian Revolution
events.desc: Khomeini returns from exile; the Shah flees. The first clerical revolution in a modern state. Political Islam goes from theory to government.

events.name: Moral Majority founded
events.desc: Jerry Falwell organizes American evangelicals into a political movement aligned with the Republican Party. The religious right arrives.

events.name: John Paul II in Poland
events.desc: The Polish pope returns home. Three million hear him at Victory Square. Be not afraid. Nine years until Solidarity topples communism.

events.name: 9/11 attacks
events.desc: Al-Qaeda hijacks four American airliners. The World Trade Center falls. Religion returns as a global security question; the War on Terror begins.

events.name: Second Vatican Council
events.desc: John XXIII opens the windows of the Church. Mass in the vernacular, ecumenism, religious liberty, engagement with the modern world. The shape of post-Tridentine Catholicism ends.

events.name: Death of God theology
events.desc: Time magazine's April 8 cover asks: Is God Dead? Thomas Altizer and William Hamilton argue that the Christian God has lost cultural reality. The high-water mark of secular confidence in the West.

polities.name: Marxist-Leninist State Atheism
polities.desc: Still formally atheist across the Warsaw Pact and China, but cracks are showing. Pope John Paul II returns to Poland in 1979; the Cultural Revolution has ended; Deng Xiaoping's reforms are beginning.

polities.name: Catholic Christianity
polities.desc: John Paul II, the first non-Italian pope in 455 years, has been elected six months earlier. Liberation theology is transforming Latin American Catholicism. Catholic charismatic renewal is reshaping parishes. In the United States, the urban Northeast remains solidly Catholic; Hispanic migration is Catholicizing the Southwest. Quebec, by contrast, has undergone the most rapid collapse of institutional Catholicism in the modern West — the Quiet Revolution of the 1960s stripped the Church of its monopoly on schools, hospitals, and civil life, and weekly Mass attendance has fallen from over 80% to below 30% in a single generation.

polities.name: Protestant Christianity
polities.desc: The Religious Right is mobilizing in the United States — the Moral Majority will be founded this year. The Bible Belt, Midwest, mountain West, and Pacific Coast are overwhelmingly Protestant. English Canada remains plurality Protestant — United Church, Anglican, Baptist — though secularization is underway. Pentecostalism is booming in Latin America, Africa, and Korea.

polities.name: Orthodox Christianity
polities.desc: Underground in the USSR but experiencing a quiet intellectual revival. Greek Orthodoxy strong. Serbian Orthodoxy will become central to the wars a decade later.

polities.name: Sunni Islam
polities.desc: The Islamic revival is global. The Grand Mosque seizure in Mecca shocks the Saudi regime. Muslim Brotherhood is spreading across the Arab world. Secular Arab nationalism is discredited.

polities.name: Shia Islam (Islamic Republic)
polities.desc: Khomeini returns to Tehran on February 1, 1979. By April, an Islamic Republic is proclaimed. The first modern state constituted on Shia clerical rule — the velayat-e faqih.

polities.name: Judaism
polities.desc: Israel-Egypt peace treaty signed at Camp David this year. Religious Zionism is rising with settlement expansion in the territories captured in 1967.

polities.name: Hinduism
polities.desc: Indira Gandhi's Emergency has ended; the RSS and its political arm (soon the BJP) are growing. Hindutva as a political force begins its long ascent.

polities.name: Buddhism
polities.desc: The Dalai Lama is in exile in India. Vietnamese Buddhism has survived the war. Western convert Buddhism is growing in Europe and North America.

polities.name: Secular West
polities.desc: Western European societies — post-Christian, demographically declining, institutionally secular. Quebec joins them: a single generation after the Quiet Revolution, Québécois identity has shifted from French-Catholic to French-secular, the most decisive religious transformation in North America since the Great Awakenings.

polities.name: Indigenous Traditions
polities.desc: Significant revitalization movements — Native American Church, African independent churches syncretizing with indigenous practice, Maori cultural renaissance. The Canadian north remains culturally distinct — Inuit and Dene communities drawing on both Christian mission heritage and pre-contact tradition.

name: The Present
desc: Secularization has proceeded in Europe, the Anglosphere, and East Asia — but not globally. Islam, Pentecostal Christianity, and Hindu nationalism are growing faster than populations. China's officially atheist Party governs a religiously reawakening society. The twenty-first century is religiously plural in ways the twentieth did not predict.

events.name: Rise of the Nones
events.desc: Religiously unaffiliated Americans surpass any single Christian denomination. The US joins Western Europe on the long glide from Christendom. A rewrite of American identity is in progress.

events.name: Abu Dhabi Abrahamic Family House
events.desc: A mosque, church, and synagogue on a single plaza commissioned by the UAE. The Abraham Accords' architectural expression — the Gulf as an interfaith laboratory.

events.name: Chinese religious revival
events.desc: Despite state atheism and sharper crackdowns under Xi, Christianity, Buddhism, folk religion, and Confucianism all grow. Estimates of Chinese Christians range from 70 to 100 million.

events.name: AI and new religious movements
events.desc: Silicon Valley's technological millenarianism — longtermism, effective altruism, the Singularity — displays the structural features of religious movements. The oldest pattern in a new substrate.

polities.name: Marxist-Leninist State Atheism (nominal)
polities.desc: The Chinese Communist Party remains officially atheist but tolerates state-registered religions. A religious revival is underway despite crackdowns on Uyghur Muslims and Tibetan Buddhists.

polities.name: Catholic Christianity
polities.desc: Pope Francis, the first Latin American pope. The Church's demographic center of gravity has shifted from Europe to the Global South. European Catholicism is in rapid decline; African and Asian Catholicism is growing. In the United States Catholics are the single largest religious group in the Northeast Catholic belt (Rhode Island, Massachusetts, Connecticut, New Jersey, New York), in Pennsylvania and Illinois, along the Hispanic Southwest (New Mexico, California), and in southern Louisiana. In Canada, New Brunswick retains its Acadian Catholic plurality.

polities.name: Protestant / Pentecostal Christianity
polities.desc: Pentecostalism is the fastest-growing form of Christianity worldwide — over 600 million adherents. African and Latin American Protestantism is reshaping the global Church. In the United States, evangelical and mainline Protestantism dominates the South, Midwest, and interior West — the Bible Belt and adjacent regions. (Utah is included here as shorthand for LDS, which is distinct but not shown as its own polity at this scale.) In Canada, the Atlantic provinces and prairies remain the country's most religiously observant — 2021 census shows Saskatchewan at 56 percent Christian, Newfoundland at 82 percent, New Brunswick at 60 percent — even as Toronto, Vancouver, and Montreal secularize.

polities.name: Orthodox Christianity
polities.desc: Russian Orthodoxy under Patriarch Kirill is aligned closely with the Putin state and the war in Ukraine. The Ukrainian Orthodox Church has split from Moscow. Georgian and Serbian churches remain politically potent.

polities.name: Sunni Islam
polities.desc: 1.8 billion Muslims globally, the vast majority Sunni. The Arab Spring's aftermath has discredited secular and Islamist alternatives alike; Salafi-Wahhabi currents remain influential.

polities.name: Shia Islam
polities.desc: Iran's Islamic Republic has entered its fifth decade. Hezbollah in Lebanon, Houthis in Yemen, Shia parties in Iraq form the regional network Tehran sponsors.

polities.name: Judaism
polities.desc: Israel's religious-secular division has grown, with Haredi and religious-Zionist populations expanding demographically. The October 7, 2023 attacks and subsequent war have reshaped the religious-political landscape.

polities.name: Hinduism
polities.desc: Narendra Modi's BJP has made Hindutva the ruling ideology of India. The Ram temple at Ayodhya was consecrated in 2024. India's secular constitutional order is under pressure.

polities.name: Sikhism
polities.desc: 30 million Sikhs globally. Punjab's politics shaped by the diaspora. Khalistan separatism remains a diplomatic flashpoint between India and Canada, the UK, and Australia.

polities.name: Buddhism
polities.desc: The Dalai Lama is 89; succession will be contested between Dharamsala and Beijing. Buddhism remains the largest religion in most of mainland Southeast Asia and is growing in the West.

polities.name: Secular / Post-Religious West
polities.desc: Most of Western Europe, Japan, much of the American West Coast and northern New England, and urban Canada. Formal religious practice is below historical norms — weekly attendance in the single digits in many places. Values are post-Christian: human rights, personal autonomy, environmental concern, scientific authority. The United States as a whole remains the most religious developed nation; the secular pattern holds mainly in the Pacific Northwest, upper New England, and the DC-federal corridor. In Canada, Quebec's Quiet Revolution legacy, cosmopolitan Ontario, and the Pacific orientation of British Columbia produce the country's most secular populations.

polities.name: Indigenous / Syncretic Traditions
polities.desc: Significant in Oceania, Amazonia, Himalayan Asia, and much of sub-Saharan Africa where they blend with Christianity or Islam. Indigenous revival movements gaining ground in several former colonies. In the Canadian north, Inuit (Nunavut), Dene (Northwest Territories), and Yukon First Nations communities retain traditional spiritualities alongside or within Christian practice — truth-and-reconciliation processes since 2008 have reinvigorated public indigenous religious expression.
